title: Oracle: OD-13 supersedes OD-5/R1001 (BL-14)
body:
Oracle ruling on the logged evidence `BL-14`, dispatched by the unattended delivery driver on base `run/web`.

**OD-13** — the owner's 2026-08-19 ruling overrules OD-5 on the whole-transcript cap, so this decision supersedes `R1001`.

- `R1001` is retired. Left standing it would sit in the requirement set (`coverage.sh` unions both design documents) directly contradicting the amended `R28`'s "the whole-transcript path is not capped", and the merged plan carrying `covers: [R1001, R28]` would remain lawfully buildable.
- No replacement oracle requirement is added: the owner already amended `R5` and `R28` in `docs/DESIGN.md` to carry the behaviour, and a duplicate id here would restate the owner's own document and split one behaviour across two.
- The measurement the reversal creates — a whole transcript spanning several sequential bundles — is named as the re-cut plan's obligation, so the new observable is counted rather than assumed.
- The merged plan `docs/plans/oracle/capped-whole-transcript-path.md` is re-cut rather than discarded: its routing module, its ratio measured on re-cut clusters, its bundle-XML `form` attribute, its per-path projection counts and its build-after-`R1000` sequencing all survive the reversal; only the cap goes.

Opened by the server-side `open-pr` workflow at the driver's request: this session cannot mint App identity (ESC-50), and an owner-authored pipeline pull request would hollow out `owner-authored.sh`.
